claims.text: The dynamic behavior of solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is primarily controlled by its effective stacking-fault energy.
Effective stacking-fault energy governs a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition between dislocation slip and mechanical twinning.
Controlled solidification can produce a homogenized FeNiCrMn microstructure with minimal initial defects.
Temperature and strain rate affect the effective stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn.
Effective stacking-fault energy mediates the relative activation of dislocation slip and mechanical twinning.
Lower-temperature and/or higher-strain-rate conditions produce a lower effective stacking-fault energy.
A lower effective stacking-fault energy promotes mechanical twinning.
Higher-temperature and/or lower-strain-rate conditions increase thermal activation and favor dislocation slip.
Twinning will be more prevalent under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions.
Dislocation slip will predominate under high-temperature, low-strain-rate conditions.
The transition between twinning and dislocation slip will coincide with measurable changes in yield strength.
The transition between twinning and dislocation slip will coincide with measurable changes in ductility.
The proposed mechanism is limited to as-solidified, homogenized Co-free FeNiCrMn within the tested temperature and strain-rate ranges.
Significant phase transformations, severe strain localization, or compositional inhomogeneity may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Twin density, dislocation density, yield strength, and ductility can be compared across temperature and strain-rate conditions to test the proposed transition.
Absence of the predicted correlation between loading conditions, deformation mechanism, effective stacking-fault energy, and mechanical response would falsify the hypothesis.
